description: Polipops is a highly committed team of university students united by our passion for STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics). Our core mission is to transform education by creating accessible and innovative learning alternatives for everyone. We are channeling our dedication into our most exciting challenge yet: developing a space mission video game. By blending strategic gameplay with scientific concepts, to prove that learning about the universe can be a great adventure.
summary:
Atlantis: Project Rover is a strategic puzzle-simulation game developed in Godot where you step into the role of a NASA researcher and engineer. Across three unique planetary orbits, you are tasked with guiding a critical space mission to success.

Rather than relying on quick reflexes, the game tests your analytical skills. You must consult a comprehensive in-game database to study environmental conditions, understand planetary hazards, and formulate the optimal strategy for each level. Analyze the data, overcome the distinct challenges of all three planets, and successfully complete Mission Atlantis!
details:
Atlantis: Project R.O.V.E.R is an interactive 5-phase space exploration strategy and flight-simulation game. It guides players (solo or in teams) through the lifecycle of a real space mission across three difficulty tiers: Earth Orbit (Easy), Moon & Mars (Medium), and Solar Orbit & Jupiter (Hard).

The game unfolds in five critical phases:

Planning: Players select a target, evaluate orbital transfer routes (balancing travel days, Δv requirements, budget, and risk), and assign team roles.

Engineering Laboratory: The core of mission prep. Players study their destination using a live 3D celestial body viewer, uncover failure risks, and assemble a modular spacecraft. They must balance structure, power (solar/battery/RTG), antennas, propulsion, and scientific instruments against strict mass, power, and data-link budgets. This phase ends with a Mission Control simulation to test components and anomaly response.

Launch & Transit: Handles lift-off and dynamic in-transit mission events.

Flight Operations: The real-time simulation. It features a dynamic 3D planetary backdrop, a clean lateral telemetry HUD, and critical branching operations based on the destination (e.g., staged Mars rover deployments, extreme heat-shield management near the Sun, or navigating Jupiter's moons).

Results: A comprehensive post-mission debrief displaying flight and engineering metrics, ending in either MISSION ACCOMPLISHED or GAME OVER.

Educational & Gameplay Benefits

Hands-On Systems Thinking: Instead of passively reading space facts, players experience real aerospace trade-offs. They learn exactly why solar panels lose efficiency at Jupiter (4% sunlight), why Mars signal delay requires autonomous computers, or why high-resolution instruments demand higher-bandwidth antennas.

Collaborative & Accessible: Supports multi-role team coordination (planning, finance, engineering, and operations) with difficulty scaling from guided learning to hidden-risk problem solving.

Immediate Visual Feedback: Every engineering decision made in the lab directly impacts flight performance, telemetry, and mission survivability during operations.

Intended Impact

Our goal is to inspire students, educators, and curious players by turning complex orbital mechanics and spacecraft engineering into an approachable, engaging experience. By letting players design, test, launch, and operate missions modeled after real NASA programs (like the Parker Solar Probe, Perseverance, and Juno), Atlantis bridges STEM education and interactive storytelling. We want to show the world how planning, testing, and teamwork make space exploration possible.

Technical Stack & Tools

Game Engine: Godot Engine 4.7 (Forward+ / Vulkan renderer) with HTML5/Web export capabilities.

Programming Language: GDScript. We built a modular architecture using autoload singletons, custom UI styling, procedural 2D telemetry/trajectory drawing, and native 3D nodes (Node3D, SubViewport, MeshInstance3D) for planetary rendering.

Assets: We heavily utilized planetary surface textures and spacecraft models from NASA 3D Resources, combined with custom 2D UI sprites and Google Fonts (Poppins).

Hardware: Standard consumer PC workstations with Vulkan-compatible graphics.

Innovation & Creativity

End-to-End Mission Continuity: Most space games focus solely on building rockets or flying them. Our project connects all five phases, meaning early choices in budgeting and component testing carry real, tangible consequences into orbital operations.

Hybrid 2D/3D Architecture: We blended responsive 2D precision flight mechanics and clean telemetry HUDs with live, rotating 3D planetary environments. This gives players clear spatial readability alongside realistic orbital visuals.

Branching Real-World Scenarios: We incorporated distinct mission profiles, like orienting a heat shield toward the Sun, or deploying a rover via sky-crane, within a unified visual language.

Design & Development Considerations

Scientific Accuracy vs. Playability: We simplified complex concepts (Δv, solar flux drop-off, communication latency, radiation shielding) into clear visual rules and UI bars that challenge players without overwhelming them.

UI Clarity and Ergonomics: We designed a non-intrusive, semi-transparent HUD and dotted trajectory guides to ensure telemetry never obscures the spacecraft or landing zone during critical maneuvers.

Performance and Accessibility: By leveraging lightweight procedural rendering, compact textures, and engine-native 3D primitives, we ensured the game runs smoothly on everyday laptops and in web browsers, maximizing accessibility.
